The requested limited-scene browser implementation is complete within its documented scope. The unchanged foundation retains 6,160 CPU tests, 118 production-browser cases, 48 tutorial/input/zoom cases and 14 native suites. These scopes overlap and are reported separately. `ui_widgets.hpp:240-250` defines the three-point `dropdownChevron`: the down ink is 5 by 2.5 units; the right ink is 2.5 by 5 units; stroke thickness is 1 unit at scale 1. Its quiet state uses TextDisabled and its highlighted state uses CheckMark. Native scaling follows the UI/DPI scale, not the font-size preference. The browser's [DecorativeChevron](../../src/ui/DecorativeChevron.tsx) uses the same centered points and stroke in a fixed decorative 10-unit SVG slot. CSS supplies the muted/accent state colors. Device pixel ratio and browser zoom rasterize those logical units; increasing the text preference does not enlarge the arrow ink. Existing dropdown/fold buttons retain their dimensions, hit areas, accessible names, focus and popup ownership. The SVG is aria-hidden, unfocusable and pointer-transparent.

The Basic/Pro header reserves the wider of both localized captions and adjusts its horizontal padding to the measured native width. This is presentation only: the actual user profile, controls and mode transitions retain their qualified behavior. Browser captures and comparison are bound as `chrome.capture` and `chrome.comparison` in the current qualification, with their actual matched-state/tolerance scope. The comparison is not a whole-image, every-theme or universal desktop-pixel claim.

Open folder remains an approved browser file-group adaptation. It occupies its own toolbar cell; the corresponding downstream position offset remains explicit instead of being concealed by moving unrelated controls. Section fold and Reset stay independent browser actions and keyboard targets. Their shared row envelope can match the native section while the fold action excludes the trailing Reset cell. Reset must not toggle the fold, and folding must not invoke Reset. The native full CollapsingHeader/overlap policy is not a reason to merge the browser hit areas.

The current implementation retains the desktop core/UI design through browser adaptations: local saved views instead of Explorer thumbnails, plain G for focused Fill with browser Find ownership, explicit numeric/color/opacity Apply/Cancel, captured selection/current-view scope, and bounded overlays instead of expensive prospective hover computation. The [tutorial references](TUTORIAL_V7_REFERENCES.md) describe the current 47-step presentation and native-owner preservation. No native/worker/transport capability or durable codec change is introduced by these arrow/header changes.

One current-build observation opened, exported and closed the pinned 256,000-record SH0 scene (8,192,000 input bytes), with independently checked output and joined owners. This is one practical observation, not measured universal capacity, a frame-rate guarantee or performance certification. The 256-MiB input and one-million loaded-preview limits remain admission ceilings; decoded data, history, GPU, recovery and output have separate admission, so an operation can be refused below those ceilings.

The practical probe's exact report is bound as `practicalProbe.report`; actual collected host, native/manifest, output and cleanup observations retain their stated scope. Logical ownership is not physical process/GPU memory. Current WebGPU/secure-context/browser permissions and admission refusals remain documented. Broader independent input/recovery cases, a concrete deployed HTTPS origin, formal capacity/performance budgets and observed assistive speech are optional evidence extensions. No Mac test, Electron/native wrapper, new remote deployment, full WCAG statement or unobserved browser/hardware support is claimed.
